standard_prerequisites.name: The Picard group of an open subscheme of a unique factorisation domain's affine space is trivial, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the standard affine charts of projective space have trivial Picard group, so invertible modules are given by cocycles for that cover.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the units of a localization as the product of the units of the base with the powers of the localizing element, and the cocycle description of invertible modules with respect to a cover
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the cocycle into a pair of data, a unit-valued part and an integral exponent part, for each overlapping pair of charts.

standard_prerequisites.name: The trivializing section of a twist of the structure sheaf on a standard chart and the corresponding cocycle
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the twisting sheaf with the class of a cocycle consisting of powers of the ratios of coordinates, matching the classification obtained.

core_obligations: Cocycle description: by the triviality of the Picard groups of the standard charts, an invertible module on projective space is given by a cocycle for the cover by those charts (proof lines 7266-7271).

Form of the cocycle: on an intersection of two charts the units of the localized coordinate ring are the product of the units of the base ring with the powers of the ratio of the two coordinates, so the cocycle is given by unit-valued and exponent-valued data (proof lines 7272-7280).

Cocycle condition: evaluating the condition on triple intersections shows that the exponent data are independent of the pair and that the unit-valued data form a coboundary, so every class is represented by a cocycle whose entries are powers of the ratios of coordinates with a single exponent (proof lines 7281-7292).

Identification with twists: the twisting sheaf of degree n has the coordinate to the n-th power as trivializing section on the n-th chart, so its cocycle is the uniform pattern of exponent n, which shows that the classification map from the integers is bijective (proof lines 7293-7301).
proof_roadmap: Use the triviality of Picard groups on the charts to write an invertible module as a cocycle, compute the units on the overlaps, and simplify the cocycle using the cocycle condition (proof lines 7266-7292).
Match the simplified cocycles with those of the twists and conclude bijectivity of the classification (proof lines 7293-7301).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Picard group of projective space over a unique factorisation domain as the integers via the twisting sheaves, with the case of a field as a special case (statement lines 7254-7264). The counted proof is a complete cocycle computation: it uses the triviality of the Picard groups of the standard charts, identifies the units on the overlaps with powers of ratios of the coordinates times base units, simplifies the cocycle using the condition on triple intersections to a single exponent, and matches the result with the cocycles of the twisting sheaves (proof lines 7266-7301). It is H2: the computation is carried out in the counted span, with the cited input being the triviality of Picard groups over unique factorisation domains.
